$comment: THE ONE REGISTRY for the sheet's knobs (ADR-114). Read by the pages (TS import, through lib/sheet/directions.ts) and by scripts/capture-subpages.mjs (readFileSync), and mirrored into the ship's armada.toml. Two readers, one record: a direction cannot be shot that the page cannot draw. TYPE IDS ARE LETTERS ONLY - the armada's filename grammar takes letters before the first dash. THE FIRST VALUE OF EVERY KNOB IS THE HOUSE: direction SB is every knob at its first value, and every other direction is an argument someone has to make against it. SA is not a knob set at all: it is the NEGATIVE POLE, today's /arcs shot once before the sheet replaced it.

head.label: Head
head.note: split = the title in the left five columns and the paragraphs opposite (Hermeus). stack = the kicker alone on the left and the title with its paragraphs stacked on the right. The owner's sentence reads both ways; the wave decides.

ordinal.label: Ordinal
ordinal.note: on = every section's head band letters 01 / 02 / … (Hermeus, Prime Intellect: ordinals as wayfinding). off = the kicker alone (the casefile's own no-ordinal ruling, ADR-066).

rules.label: Rules
rules.note: sheet = two full-height hairlines at the band's edges plus a seam between sections (Tensorlake, Kindled). seams = the seams alone; the page's edges are air.

card.label: Cards
card.note: stack = the console's flashcards stack on scroll under a sticky panel (the proof stack's mechanic). grid = the same cards in a static two-column grid.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.note: axis = a horizontal dated axis with the sessions seated on it at their dates (Hermeus roadmap). rail = a vertical date rail with the sessions opposite (Hermeus detail) — also the phone's own layout.

directions.name: Old arcs
directions.question: the negative pole: what the owner said looks bad, byte-identical, so every check that names it can be shown to fail it
directions.shape: a centred hero over a gutter grid of chamfered posters, no page rules

directions.name: House
directions.question: does the sheet at its own values read as one instrument across six pages, both themes and both viewports?
directions.shape: the ruled sheet: split head, ordinals, full-height rules, the pile, the axis

directions.name: Seams
directions.question: does the page still read as seated with the full-height rules gone and only the seams left?
directions.shape: the same sheet with its two long rules erased

directions.name: Editorial
directions.question: does the head read better stacked on the right with no ordinals, or does the page lose its wayfinding?
directions.shape: kicker left, title and paragraphs stacked right, no section numerals

directions.name: Grid
directions.question: does a static grid of flashcards and a vertical date rail say the same thing as the pile and the axis, with less motion?
directions.shape: cards in two columns, the sessions on a rail

wave.note: 4 directions x 6 types x 2 themes at the default viewport, one still per section; laptop for SB first. 1920x1247 is the owner's own window; 1280x720 is the binding one.
